# The built-in patterns as a caller has them: all of them at once, which is what
# AllBuiltinPatterns hands out.
#
# A value one pattern locates whole can be one another locates in part — a
# stateless installation token carries a JWT, and an access key ID can be
# written inside either without ending it — so what matters here is that the
# patterns do not take pieces out of each other's values, and that a line
# holding several kinds of credential loses all of them. The block that closes
# this file is where the second of those stops holding, and says why.

patterns: default

case:     a stateless installation token is one value, not a token and a jwt
in:       token=ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      token=«github-token»

case:     a stateless user access token is one value, not a token and a jwt
in:       token=ghu_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      token=«github-token»

case:     a personal access token prefix in the stateless form leaves the prefix behind
in:       token=ghp_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      token=ghp_123456_«jwt»

case:     a personal access token and a jwt on one line
in:       token=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      token=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     a jwt before a personal access token
in:       jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef token=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      jwt=«jwt» token=«github-token»

case:     a private key and a personal access token on separate lines
in:       -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n0123456789abcdef\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\ntoken=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «private-key»\ntoken=«github-token»

case:     a stateless installation token beside a jwt of its own
in:       ghs_1_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef and eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ4eXoifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token» and «jwt»

case:     every kind of credential this library knows
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz github_pat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 out:      «github-token» «github-token» «jwt» «aws-access-key-id» «aws-access-key-id» aws_secret_access_key=«aws-secret-access-key» «slack-token» «gitlab-token» «google-api-key» «openai-api-key» «openrouter-api-key» «anthropic-api-key» «stripe-secret-key» «stripe-publishable-key» «stripe-webhook-signing-secret» «pypi-api-token» «npm-access-token» «sendgrid-api-key» «sentry-auth-token» «linear-api-key» «notion-api-token» «hashicorp-vault-token» «grafana-service-account-token» «supabase-access-token» «supabase-publishable-key» «supabase-secret-key» «rubygems-api-key» «cloudflare-api-token» «cloudflare-api-key» «huggingface-user-access-token» «crates-io-token» «crates-io-token» «databricks-personal-access-token» «databricks-oauth-client-secret» «digitalocean-token» «postman-api-key» «pulumi-access-token» «sourcegraph-access-token» «planetscale-token» «airtable-personal-access-token» «heroku-api-token» «doppler-auth-token» «shopify-access-token» «shopify-app-secret-key» «circleci-api-token» «circleci-api-token» «age-secret-key» «1password-service-account-token» «docker-personal-access-token» «replicate-api-token» «resend-api-key» «paddle-api-key» «sonarqube-token» «dynatrace-token» «groq-api-key» «xai-api-key» «posthog-personal-api-key» «newrelic-user-key» «fly-io-access-token» «hcp-terraform-api-token» «buildkite-token» «neon-api-key» «pinecone-api-key» «netlify-auth-token» «private-key»

# The two halves of an AWS access key, which are two patterns rather than one:
# the ID is an identifier a log is kept for and the secret is what authenticates
# with it. A caller holding both redacts both, and the names stay in the text
# either way — the secret's name is what the pattern reads it by, so redacting
# it would take away what says which credential was there.

case:     both halves of an aws access key in a shared credentials file
in:       [default]\naws_access_key_id = AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\naws_secret_access_key = 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      [default]\naws_access_key_id = «aws-access-key-id»\naws_secret_access_key = «aws-secret-access-key»

case:     both halves in the json an assume-role call prints
in:       {"AccessKeyId":"ASIA0123456789ABCDEF","SecretAccessKey":"0123456789abcdef0123456789ab+/ef01234567"}
out:      {"AccessKeyId":"«aws-access-key-id»","SecretAccessKey":"«aws-secret-access-key»"}

# Shopify's two credentials, which share an opening, a separator, a count and an
# alphabet and are told apart by the two characters naming the kind. They are two
# patterns because they are held by different parties and leak to different
# effect, and a redactor keying on the name can write that distinction only
# because the boundary hands it one.

case:     an access token and the app secret key in one configuration
in:       SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN=shpat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\nSHOPIFY_API_SECRET=shpss_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN=«shopify-access-token»\nSHOPIFY_API_SECRET=«shopify-app-secret-key»

case:     an access token and an app secret key with nothing between them
in:       shpat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefshpss_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «shopify-access-token»«shopify-app-secret-key»

case:     a fine grained token holding a run that opens like a header
in:       github_pat_0123456789abcdefeyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghij
out:      «github-token»

case:     no pattern finds anything in a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.github.com/user
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.github.com/user

case:     no pattern finds anything in prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# Where one kind of credential is written inside another, and where one ends
# exactly where the other begins. No pattern may take a piece out of another's
# value, and none may leave a piece of its own behind.

case:     a jwt whose payload decodes to a personal access token
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMiLCJ0b2tlbiI6ImdocF8wMTIzNDU2Nzg5YWJjZGVmZ2hpamtsbW5vcHFyc3R1dnd4eXoifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «jwt»

case:     a jwt directly followed by a personal access token
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdefghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «jwt»

case:     a personal access token directly followed by a jwt
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzeyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     a jwt whose signature opens like a token prefix
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «jwt»

case:     a jwt whose header segment carries a token prefix before it
in:       ghp_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      ghp_«jwt»

case:     an access key id written where the base64 of a key stands
in:       -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nAKIA0123456789ABCDEF\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----
out:      «private-key»

# A dot is not base64, so what is written between two boundaries is not always
# a body, and the pattern that does read it is the one that locates it.

case:     a jwt written where the base64 of a key would stand
in:       -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\neyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----
out:      -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n«jwt»\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----

case:     a fine grained token whose second run opens like a header
in:       github_pat_0123456789abcdefABCDEF_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLM
out:      «github-token»

case:     a stateless installation token whose app id is a classic token body
in:       ghs_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     a stateless installation token whose inner jwt names alg none
in:       ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     a stateless installation token, a fine grained token and a jwt on one line
in:       ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef github_pat_0123456789abcdefABCDEF_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVW eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token» «github-token» «jwt»

case:     a json body holding a classic token, a fine grained token and a jwt
in:       {"classic":"ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz","fine":"github_pat_0123456789abcdefABCDEF_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVW","jwt":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"classic":"«github-token»","fine":"«github-token»","jwt":"«jwt»"}

case:     a token in an authorization header and a jwt in a cookie on one line
in:       Authorization: token ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz; Cookie: session=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: token «github-token»; Cookie: session=«jwt»

case:     a url carrying a token in its userinfo and a jwt in its query
in:       https://x-access-token:ghs_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz@example.com/callback?id_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      https://x-access-token:«github-token»@example.com/callback?id_token=«jwt»

case:     a jwt and a token with a single dot between them
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef.ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «jwt».«github-token»

case:     a token and a jwt with a single dot between them
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token».«jwt»

# An access key ID inside a value of another kind. The alphabet a key is
# written in — uppercase letters and digits — is inside the alphabet of a
# GitHub token body and inside base64url, so a key can be written into either
# without ending it, and the AWS pattern locates it there whether or not the
# characters around it are a credential of their own. Where they are, the two
# spans overlap and are redacted as one; the surrounding value is what starts
# earliest, so that is what the redaction is attributed to.

case:     an access key id inside a classic token body
in:       ghp_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     an access key id inside the app id of a stateless installation token
in:       ghs_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     an access key id inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.AKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «jwt»

case:     an access key id directly after a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdefAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «jwt»

case:     an access key id directly after a classic token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «github-token»

case:     an access key id and a jwt with a single dot between them
in:       AKIA0123456789ABCDEF.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «aws-access-key-id».«jwt»

case:     an access key id in an environment file beside a github token
in:       AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Slack token beside the other kinds, and inside them. A Slack body is read
# as letters, digits and the hyphen its parts are joined with, so an access key
# ID can be written into one without ending it and is located there as well;
# the two values overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to what starts
# earliest. The underscore and the dot end a Slack body instead, which is what
# keeps a GitHub token and a JWT written after a prefix out of it — and leaves
# the prefix and the identifier in front of them in the text, which authenticate
# nothing on their own.

case:     a slack token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       slack=xoxb-0123456789ab-0123456789abc-0123456789abcdefghijklmn github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      slack=«slack-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a slack token body
in:       xoxb-0123456789ab-AKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «slack-token»

case:     an access key id directly after a slack token
in:       xoxb-0123456789ab-0123456789abcdefghijklmnAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «slack-token»

case:     a github token after a slack prefix, which the underscore keeps apart
in:       xoxb-0123456789ab_ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      xoxb-0123456789ab_«github-token»

case:     a jwt directly after a slack token, which the dot keeps apart
in:       xoxb-0123456789ab-0123456789abcdefgh.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «slack-token».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding one of each
in:       SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-0123456789ab-0123456789abc-0123456789abcdefghijklmn\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=«slack-token»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# The other direction: a Slack prefix written against the end of an access key
# ID rather than a key written into a Slack body. A prefix standing behind a
# letter or a digit opens nothing, so the key is redacted and the bot token
# beside it comes through whole and would authenticate a request as it stands.
# That is what the case below shows, and it is here to be looked up rather than
# arrived at: neither pattern's own file states what the two of them come to
# when both are enabled.
#
# It is here for what comes after that, which no out field can state. Redacting
# the key puts characters that are neither a letter nor a digit where its last
# one stood, so the prefix a letter had closed is open to a second pass and the
# token is redacted then. Masking is not idempotent, and the doc comment on
# Mask says so; checkSecondPass (properties_test.go) is what holds a second
# pass here, and this is the input it was written against.

case:     a slack prefix written against the end of an access key id
in:       AKIA0123456789ABCDEFxoxb-0123456789ab-0123456789abc-0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:      «aws-access-key-id»xoxb-0123456789ab-0123456789abc-0123456789abcdefghijklmn

# A GitLab token beside the others. Its body is read in the base64url alphabet
# and to a count the kind fixes, which is what makes it behave unlike the Slack
# body beside it: a value written inside a GitLab body is located there too and
# the two are redacted as one, but a value written after one begins where the
# count ends, so both are located and neither takes a piece out of the other.
# The dot ends a body, which is what keeps a JWT written after a token out of
# it.

case:     a gitlab token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       gitlab=glpat-0123456789abcdefghij github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      gitlab=«gitlab-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a gitlab token body
in:       glpat-AKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «gitlab-token»

case:     an access key id where a gitlab token body ends
in:       glpat-0123456789abcdefghijAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «gitlab-token»«aws-access-key-id»

case:     a github token after a gitlab prefix, which the body alphabet draws in
in:       glpat-ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «gitlab-token»

case:     a jwt directly after a gitlab token, which the dot keeps apart
in:       glpat-0123456789abcdefghij.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «gitlab-token».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding a gitlab token among the others
in:       GITLAB_TOKEN=glpat-0123456789abcdefghij\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      GITLAB_TOKEN=«gitlab-token»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Google API key beside the others, and inside them. A key is thirty-nine
# characters of base64url and its prefix is written in that same alphabet, so it
# can stand inside any value read in an alphabet as wide — a GitHub token body,
# a GitLab body, the signature of a JWT — and is located there as well; the two
# spans overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to whichever starts
# earliest. Where it is the count that ends a key rather than a separator,
# whatever is written straight after one is a value of its own, and both go.

case:     a google api key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       google=AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      google=«google-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     a google api key inside a classic github token body
in:       ghp_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      «github-token»

case:     a google api key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      «jwt»

case:     a google api key inside a gitlab oauth application secret
in:       gloas-AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy0123456789abcdefghijklmno
out:      «gitlab-token»

case:     a google api key where a gitlab token body ends
in:       glpat-0123456789abcdefghijAIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      «gitlab-token»«google-api-key»

case:     a google api key directly after a classic github token

# An OpenAI API key beside the others, and inside them. A key is the prefix, a
# run of base64url characters, and the marker T3BlbkFJ somewhere inside that
# run, so it can stand inside any value read in an alphabet as wide — a GitLab
# body, the signature of a JWT — and is located there as well; the two spans
# overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to whichever starts earliest. The
# same width works the other way round, and what ends a key is where its run
# ends rather than a count, so a value of another kind written inside a key or
# straight after it falls inside the key's own span rather than beside it. That
# is how a classic GitHub token body behaves above and not how the GitLab and
# Google counts do. A dot ends the run, which is what keeps a JWT written after
# a key apart from it.

case:     an openai api key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       openai=sk-proj-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      openai=«openai-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an openai api key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.sk-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef
out:      «jwt»

case:     an openai api key inside a gitlab oauth application secret
in:       gloas-sk-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234
out:      «gitlab-token»

case:     a google api key inside an openai api key run
in:       sk-proj-AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef
out:      «openai-api-key»

case:     an access key id written straight after an openai api key
in:       sk-proj-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdefAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «openai-api-key»

case:     a jwt directly after an openai api key, which the dot keeps apart
in:       sk-proj-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «openai-api-key».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding an openai api key among the others
in:       OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      OPENAI_API_KEY=«openai-api-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# An Anthropic API key beside the others, and inside them. A key opens sk-, as
# an OpenAI key does, and what tells the two apart is what follows: ant-, a kind
# and a hyphen for one, a run carrying the marker T3BlbkFJ for the other. So
# neither pattern is troubled by the other's values, and a body carrying those
# eight characters is a key to both at once — one redaction is made of it, and
# it is attributed to whichever of the two the registry names first. Behind the
# prefix a key is base64url read to the end of its run, so a value of another
# kind written inside one or straight after it falls inside the key's own span
# rather than beside it, as it does with an OpenAI key and not with the GitLab
# and Google counts. A dot ends the run, which is what keeps a JWT written after
# a key apart from it.

case:     an anthropic api key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       anthropic=sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      anthropic=«anthropic-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an anthropic api key and an openai api key on one line
in:       ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef
out:      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=«anthropic-api-key» OPENAI_API_KEY=«openai-api-key»

case:     an anthropic api key whose body carries the marker an openai key is read by
in:       sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789aT3BlbkFJ3456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      «anthropic-api-key»

case:     a google api key inside an anthropic api key body
in:       sk-ant-api03-AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      «anthropic-api-key»

case:     an access key id written straight after an anthropic api key
in:       sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «anthropic-api-key»

case:     an anthropic api key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      «jwt»

case:     a jwt directly after an anthropic api key, which the dot keeps apart
in:       sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «anthropic-api-key».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding an anthropic api key among the others

out:      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=«anthropic-api-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A PyPI API token beside the others, and inside them. Behind its prefix a
# token is base64url read to the end of its run, as an OpenAI or an Anthropic
# key is, so a value of another kind written inside one or straight after it
# falls inside the token's own span rather than beside it. A GitLab body ends
# at a count instead, so a token written where one ends is a value of its own
# and both go. A dot ends the run, which is what keeps a JWT written after a
# token apart from it — and a token written where a JWT's own signature stands
# falls inside that JWT's span, which starts earlier, so the redaction is
# attributed to the JWT.

case:     a pypi api token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       pypi=pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      pypi=«pypi-api-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

out:      «jwt»

out:      «pypi-api-token»

# An npm access token beside the others, and inside them. A body is base62 read
# to the end of its run: the letters of both cases and the digits, which is the
# alphabet a classic GitHub token body is read in and narrower than the
# base64url the OpenAI and Anthropic bodies are. So a value written in an
# alphabet as narrow can stand inside an npm body and is located there as well;
# the two spans overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to whichever starts
# earliest. The underscore is what ends a body rather than a count, so a value
# whose own prefix carries one begins after the run it interrupted — and the two
# still overlap, because that run reached the letters standing in front of the
# underscore.

case:     an npm access token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       npm=npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      npm=«npm-access-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside an npm access token body
in:       npm_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef
out:      «npm-access-token»

case:     a google api key inside an npm access token body
in:       npm_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      «npm-access-token»

case:     an npm access token inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «jwt»

case:     a classic github token written straight after an npm access token
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «npm-access-token»

case:     an npm access token written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyznpm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «github-token»

case:     a jwt directly after an npm access token, which the dot keeps apart
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «npm-access-token».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding an npm access token among the others

# The same reading against a PyPI token, which is where base62 standing inside
# base64url is read the other way round. A PyPI body admits the underscore an
# npm prefix closes with, so a whole npm access token can be written inside one
# without ending it and is located there as well, and a PyPI run does not stop
# where an npm access token begins behind it. Whichever way the two are written,
# the spans overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to whichever starts
# earliest — nothing of either is left in the text, which is what separates this
# pairing from the Stripe one the end of this file states.

case:     an npm access token inside a pypi api token body
in:       pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmcnpm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdef
out:      «pypi-api-token»

case:     an npm access token written straight after a pypi api token
in:       pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefnpm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «pypi-api-token»

case:     a pypi api token written straight after an npm access token
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzpypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «npm-access-token»

# Where the GitHub and JWT patterns disagree about a stateless installation
# token. The GitHub pattern asks for an app id, a single underscore, and a JWT
# whose every segment holds at least one character; the JWT pattern asks a
# token only for its segments, empty or not. So a stateless token the first
# declines can still be a JWT to the second, and what is then left in the text
# is the ghs_ and the app id, which authenticate nothing on their own.

case:     a stateless installation token whose jwt has an empty signature
in:       ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.
out:      ghs_123456_«jwt»

case:     a stateless installation token with no app id
in:       ghs__eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      ghs__«jwt»

case:     a stateless installation token whose app id is separated by two underscores
in:       ghs_123456__eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      ghs_123456__«jwt»

case:     a stateless installation token carrying an encrypted jwt
in:       ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJkaXIiLCJlbmMiOiJBMTI4R0NNIn0.0123456789abcdef.0123456789.0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

# And the shapes no pattern takes anything from. Each of the three shapes below
# is a GitHub credential the GitHub and JWT patterns each decline for a reason
# of their own, stated in the files beside this one, and that the AWS pattern
# has nothing to say about at all; what only the patterns together show is what
# is left in the text when none of them steps in, and that is not the same for
# the three.
#
# The first is harmless. A stateless token cut before its second dot carries no
# signature, which the GitHub pattern declines it for and which leaves the JWT
# pattern a segment short of a token. It is the shape a log line cut to a
# column limit leaves, and it comes through whole: an app id, a header and a
# payload, none of which authenticates a request.
#
# The second is not. A JOSE header written with a tab, a carriage return or a
# newline between the brace and the first member name does not open with the ey
# both patterns search for, so neither of them sees a candidate at all — and a
# whole stateless installation token, signature and all, comes through in the
# clear and would authenticate a request as it stands. The space JSON allows in
# that place is admitted by both, so those three are what is left over, and the
# compact JSON an encoder emits carries none of them. The case below is the
# tab; builtin_github_token.txt states the other two. The case is here because
# neither reason states what the two of them come to when both patterns are
# enabled, and a credential surviving whole is what a reader has to be able to
# look up rather than arrive at.
#
# The third leaves the credential whole as well, with one byte standing in the
# middle of it. A run of base64url characters ends at a line break, so a token
# written across one leaves the GitHub pattern short of the segments it asks
# for and the JWT pattern short of a token, and neither locates anything: every
# byte of the token is in the text, and a newline is the whole of what stands
# between them. builtin_jwt.txt states that a JWT broken across two lines is
# not located; what only the two patterns together show is that a stateless
# installation token broken the same way is not located either, by either of
# them, and that taking the break out gives a credential that would
# authenticate a request. The case below breaks it after the dot that ends the
# header.

case:     a stateless installation token cut before its signature
in:       ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ
out:      ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ

case:     a stateless installation token whose header is written with a tab after the brace
in:       ghs_123456_ewkiYWxnIjoiSFMyNTYifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      ghs_123456_ewkiYWxnIjoiSFMyNTYifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef

case:     a stateless installation token written across a line break
in:       ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.\neyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      ghs_123456_eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.\neyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef

# A SendGrid key beside the other kinds, and inside them. A key is three
# dot-separated base64url segments, which is a JWT's shape as well, and the two
# patterns still read it apart: a JWT is anchored on the ey a JOSE header opens
# with, and SG is not that. The out field below is what says so — were both to
# locate the same span, the value would be attributed to the JWT pattern, which
# AllBuiltinPatterns reports first.
#
# Inside a key, the two segments are read in base64url and to a fixed count, so
# an access key ID fits an identifier and a Google API key fits a secret; both
# are located there as well, the values overlap and are redacted as one,
# attributed to what starts earliest. Behind a key nothing is swallowed, which
# is what the count being a count buys: a token written straight after one keeps
# a redaction of its own where a Stripe key's run would have reached into it.

case:     a sendgrid key is one value, not a key and a jwt
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a sendgrid key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       sendgrid=SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      sendgrid=«sendgrid-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a sendgrid key identifier
in:       SG.AKIA0123456789ABCDEF01.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a google api key inside a sendgrid key secret
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.AIza0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a github token directly after a sendgrid key
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789aghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»«github-token»

case:     a jwt directly after a sendgrid key, which the dot keeps apart
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «sendgrid-api-key».«jwt»

case:     a sendgrid key in an environment file beside a stripe key and an access key id
in:       SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      SENDGRID_API_KEY=«sendgrid-api-key»\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»

# A Sentry auth token beside the other kinds, and inside one. The token with a
# hexadecimal body is read to an exact count, so a value written straight after
# one is reached and keeps a redaction of its own. An organization token's two
# segments are base64, which admits the letters and digits an access key ID and
# a Google API key are written in, so either can be written into one without
# ending it and is located there as well; the values overlap and are redacted as
# one, attributed to what starts earliest.
#
# In front of a token the underscore its prefix closes with is what a value of
# another kind is stopped by. An npm body is read to the end of its run and the
# six characters in front of a Sentry separator belong to that run, so the npm
# token's span reaches into the Sentry prefix and stops at the underscore behind
# it — the two spans overlap there and both values go.

case:     a sentry token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       sentry=sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      sentry=«sentry-auth-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside an organization payload
in:       sntrys_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ab_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     a google api key inside an organization secret
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_AIza0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     a github token directly after a sentry token
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «sentry-auth-token»«github-token»

case:     a sentry token written against the end of an npm access token
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzsntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «npm-access-token»

case:     a sentry token in an environment file beside a stripe key and an access key id
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=«sentry-auth-token»\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»

# A Linear API key beside the other kinds, and inside them. A body is base62
# read to the end of its run, as an npm body is, so a value written in an
# alphabet as narrow can stand inside one and is located there as well; the two
# spans overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to whichever starts
# earliest. The underscore is what ends a body rather than a count, so a value
# whose own prefix carries one begins after the run it interrupted — and the two
# still overlap, because that run reached the letters standing in front of the
# underscore. A dot ends a body as well, which is what keeps a JWT written
# straight after a key a value of its own.
#
# Read the other way round it is the prefix's own two underscores that matter.
# base64url admits them where base62 does not, so a whole key can be written
# inside a JWT signature or a PyPI token body without ending either, and the
# spans overlap there too.

case:     a linear key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       linear=lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123 github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      linear=«linear-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a linear key body
in:       lin_api_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdefghij
out:      «linear-api-key»

case:     a google api key inside a linear key body
in:       lin_api_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy0
out:      «linear-api-key»

case:     a linear key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      «jwt»

case:     a linear key inside a pypi api token body
in:       pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmclin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdef
out:      «pypi-api-token»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a linear key
in:       lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «linear-api-key»

case:     a linear key written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzlin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      «github-token»

case:     a jwt directly after a linear key, which the dot keeps apart
in:       lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «linear-api-key».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding a linear key among the others
in:       LINEAR_API_KEY=lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      LINEAR_API_KEY=«linear-api-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Stripe key written against the end of a Linear key, which is the shape the
# block closing this file states of an npm access token and ends the same way. A
# Linear body is read to the end of its run and the sk opening the Stripe prefix
# is two characters of that run, so the key's span reaches into the prefix and
# stops at the underscore behind them. The Linear key is redacted and takes the
# sk away with it, and the whole random part of a live secret key stays in the
# text. Written the other way round the Stripe body reaches three characters
# into the Linear prefix and stops at its underscore, so the two spans overlap
# and both values go.

case:     a stripe key written against the end of a linear key
in:       lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «linear-api-key»

case:     a linear key written against the end of a stripe key
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567lin_api_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

# A Stripe key beside the other kinds, and inside them. Both halves of the
# format are here — the case named "a google api key inside a stripe key body"
# is written with a publishable key and the rest with secret ones — because what
# the cases are about is the body, which the two share. A body is written in
# letters and digits alone, so an access key ID and a Google API key can each be
# written into one without ending it and are located there as well; the values
# overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to what starts earliest. The
# underscore ends a body instead, which is what lets a GitHub token written
# after a key be reached at all — the key's run reaches three characters into
# the token's own prefix and stops at the underscore behind them, so the two
# spans overlap there and are redacted as one.
#
# The block closing this file is the other direction, and is where a value
# beside a Stripe key costs one of them.

case:     a stripe key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       stripe=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567 github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      stripe=«stripe-secret-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a stripe key body
in:       sk_live_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a google api key inside a stripe key body
in:       pk_live_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      «stripe-publishable-key»

case:     a github token directly after a stripe key
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a jwt directly after a stripe key, which the dot keeps apart
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «stripe-secret-key».«jwt»

case:     a stripe key in an environment file beside a github token and an access key id
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# The other direction: a Stripe prefix written against the end of a value of
# another kind rather than a value written into a Stripe body. A prefix standing
# behind a letter or a digit opens nothing, unless the run of them is long
# enough to have been a key's own body — a key written against a key is a key,
# which builtin_stripe_secret_key.go argues — and an access key ID leaves a run
# shorter than that. So the access key ID is redacted and the secret key beside
# it comes through whole and would authenticate a request as it stands. That is
# what the case below shows, and it is here to be looked up rather than arrived
# at: neither pattern's own file states what the two of them come to when both
# are enabled. The Notion case further down is this shape with a long enough run
# in front of the prefix, and does not end this way.
#
# It is the same shape the Slack case above it has, and it ends the same way,
# which no out field can state. Redacting the access key ID puts characters that
# are neither a letter nor a digit where its last one stood, so the prefix a
# letter had closed is open to a second pass and the key is redacted then.
# Masking is not idempotent, and the doc comment on Mask says so.

case:     a stripe prefix written against the end of an access key id
in:       AKIA0123456789ABCDEFsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «aws-access-key-id»sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

# The same shape with an npm access token in front of the Stripe key, which ends
# differently and worse. An npm body is read to the end of its run and the sk
# opening the Stripe prefix is two characters of that run, so the token's span
# reaches into the prefix and stops at the underscore behind them. The npm
# access token is redacted and takes the sk away with it; what is left is no
# Stripe prefix at all, and the whole random part of a live secret key stays in
# the text.
#
# What the block above closes with does not hold here. There the redaction put a
# character that is neither a letter nor a digit where the prefix had been
# closed off by one, so a second pass reached the key. Here the prefix itself is
# gone, and no pass will find it again: masking the first case below a second
# time gives back exactly what masking it once gave. That is not something an
# out field can state, which is why it is written here.
#
# The two cases after it are the other direction and the same line written with
# a space in it. Written the other way round the Stripe body reaches three
# characters into the npm prefix and stops at its underscore, so the two spans
# overlap and both values go; with a space between them there is nothing to
# reach into and both go as well. It is the abutment in the first case alone
# that costs a credential, and neither pattern's own file states it — it takes
# the npm reading of a run and the byte the Stripe scan demands in front of a
# prefix together to arrive at.
#
# The middle case concatenates a Stripe body and the three letters an npm prefix
# opens with into twenty-seven characters behind sk_live_, which is the format
# of a Highnote live secret key: GitHub's push protection declines the line, and
# declines the restricted and test mode spellings of it too. It was allowed
# through as the false positive it is rather than written around, because what
# the corpus states is not the secret scanner's to narrow.

case:     a stripe key written against the end of an npm access token
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «npm-access-token»

case:     an npm access token written against the end of a stripe key
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     an npm access token and a stripe key with a space between them
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «npm-access-token» «stripe-secret-key»

# A Notion token beside the others, and inside them. A body is base62 read to a
# fixed count: the letters of both cases and the digits, which is the alphabet a
# classic GitHub token body and an npm access token body are read in. So a value
# written in an alphabet as narrow can stand inside a Notion body without ending
# it and is located there as well; the two spans overlap and are redacted as
# one, attributed to whichever starts earliest.
#
# Behind a token the count is what decides. A value written straight after one
# keeps a redaction of its own, where a run read to its end would have reached
# into it — and written the other way round, a run that does read to its end
# reaches three characters into a Notion prefix and stops at the underscore
# behind them, so the two overlap there and both go.

case:     a notion token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       notion=ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      notion=«notion-api-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a notion token body
in:       ntn_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      «notion-api-token»

case:     a google api key inside a notion token body
in:       ntn_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy0123456
out:      «notion-api-token»

case:     a notion token inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «jwt»

case:     a notion token written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «github-token»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a notion token
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «notion-api-token»«github-token»

case:     a jwt directly after a notion token, which the dot keeps apart
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «notion-api-token».«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding a notion token among the others
in:       NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      NOTION_TOKEN=«notion-api-token»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Stripe prefix written against the end of a Notion token, which is the shape
# the case named "a stripe prefix written against the end of an access key id"
# has and is not the way that one ends. What the Stripe scan asks in front of a
# prefix is that no letter and no digit stand there — and then, where one does,
# how long the run of them is. A run long enough to have been a key's own body
# is read as a key written against a key rather than as a prefix closing a word,
# which builtin_stripe_secret_key.go argues and which is what keeps every key of
# a run written with nothing between them. A Notion body is read to a count far
# past that length, so the secret key here is located in the same pass as the
# token in front of it and neither is left in the text.
#
# Neither pattern's own file states what the two come to together, which is why
# the case is here — and what this case and that one state between them is where
# the two shapes part: the run in front of the sk, not the kind of value that
# left it.

case:     a stripe prefix written against the end of a notion token
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «notion-api-token»«stripe-secret-key»

# A Vault token beside the values it can be written inside of, and inside. The
# two cases the Vault file states as its own over-matching open the block: the
# Vault pattern reaches the tail of a JWT and of a SendGrid key from the dot
# onward, the pattern that issued the value reaches the value whole, and the two
# spans merge into it. The cases after them are the values a Vault body can hold
# and the tokens written against either end of one, where a body read to the end
# of its run reaches into what follows and a base62 body reaches into a Vault
# prefix. Every one of them comes out as a single redaction.

case:     a jwt whose payload closes on a vault prefix
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQhvs.0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «jwt»

case:     a sendgrid key whose first segment closes on a vault prefix
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012hvb.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     an access key id inside a vault token body
in:       hvs.AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456
out:      «hashicorp-vault-token»

case:     a google api key inside a vault token body
in:       hvs.AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      «hashicorp-vault-token»

case:     a vault token written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzhvs.0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «github-token»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a vault token
in:       hvs.0123456789abcdef01234567ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «hashicorp-vault-token»

case:     a vault token and a jwt on one line
in:       VAULT_TOKEN=hvs.0123456789abcdef01234567 jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      VAULT_TOKEN=«hashicorp-vault-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an environment file holding a vault token among the others
in:       VAULT_TOKEN=hvs.0123456789abcdef01234567\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      VAULT_TOKEN=«hashicorp-vault-token»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Grafana service account token beside the others, and the credentials that
# can be written inside one. A secret is thirty-two base62 characters, which is
# room for an access key ID at twenty and for a Google API key at thirty-nine
# only because a Google body is base64url and may carry the underscore a token
# divides its secret from its checksum by. Either is located where it stands
# and the token is located around it; the spans overlap and are redacted as one,
# attributed to whichever starts earliest.
#
# Behind a token the count is what decides, as it is behind an access key ID:
# what is written after the forty-sixth character keeps a redaction of its own
# or none.

case:     a grafana token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       grafana=glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567 github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      grafana=«grafana-service-account-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a grafana secret
in:       glsa_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ab_01234567
out:      «grafana-service-account-token»

case:     a google api key inside a grafana secret
in:       glsa_AIza0123456789abcdef0123456789ab_01234567
out:      «grafana-service-account-token»

case:     a grafana token inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567
out:      «jwt»

case:     a grafana token written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzglsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567
out:      «github-token»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a grafana token
in:       glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «grafana-service-account-token»«github-token»

case:     a notion token written straight after a grafana token
in:       glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «grafana-service-account-token»«notion-api-token»

case:     an environment file holding a grafana token among the others
in:       GRAFANA_TOKEN=glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      GRAFANA_TOKEN=«grafana-service-account-token»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Stripe prefix written against the end of a Grafana token, which is the shape
# the case named "a stripe prefix written against the end of an access key id"
# takes and ends the same way. A Grafana token closes with an underscore and a
# short segment behind it, and an underscore is no character a Stripe body is
# written with — so the run of letters and digits standing in front of the sk is
# that segment alone, which is shorter than a body, and the prefix behind it is
# read as one closing a word. The token is redacted and the secret key beside it
# comes through whole and would authenticate a request as it stands. Neither
# pattern's own file states what the two come to together, which is why the case
# is here.
#
# No out field can state how it ends, any more than it can for that case:
# redacting the token puts characters that are neither a letter nor a digit
# where its last one stood, so the prefix is open to a second pass and the key
# is redacted then. Masking is not idempotent, and the doc comment on Mask says
# so.

case:     a stripe prefix written against the end of a grafana token
in:       glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «grafana-service-account-token»sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a stripe key a space away from a grafana token
in:       glsa_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_01234567 sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «grafana-service-account-token» «stripe-secret-key»

# The Supabase access token beside the others, in both the forms it is issued
# in. A body is written in lowercase hexadecimal digits and nothing else, and
# the cases named "an access key id written into a supabase body" and "a google
# api key written into a supabase body" are what that comes to: where a Grafana
# secret is base62 and holds either of those whole, an uppercase letter ends a
# Supabase body rather than standing inside one, so each run is redacted as what
# it is and the prefix written in front of it stays in the text.
#
# Behind a token the count is what decides, as it is behind an access key ID and
# a Grafana token: what is written after the forty-fourth character keeps a
# redaction of its own or none.

case:     a supabase token beside a github token and a jwt
in:       supabase=sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      supabase=«supabase-access-token» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id written into a supabase body
in:       sbp_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef0123
out:      sbp_«aws-access-key-id»0123456789abcdef0123

case:     a google api key written into a supabase body
in:       sbp_AIza0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123
out:      sbp_«google-api-key»3

case:     a supabase token inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «jwt»

case:     a supabase token written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzsbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «github-token»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a supabase token
in:       sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «supabase-access-token»«github-token»

case:     an oauth token written straight after a notion token
in:       ntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdsbp_oauth_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «notion-api-token»«supabase-access-token»

case:     an environment file holding a supabase token among the others
in:       SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=«supabase-access-token»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# The three prefixes Supabase writes credentials with, which are three patterns
# and agree on their first two characters. sbp_ carries the p of a personal access
# token where a project key carries the underscore that opens the word naming its
# kind, so the third character is what decides between them; the anon key those
# project keys replaced is a JWT signed with the project's secret, which the JWT
# pattern reads. The first case is what a project's environment file looks like
# with all four in it, and the three after it are the prefixes written against one
# another with nothing between.

case:     an access token, an anon key and both project keys in one environment file
in:       SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567\nSUPABASE_ANON_KEY=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJyb2xlIjoiYW5vbiJ9.0123456789abcdef\nSUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567\nSUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=«supabase-access-token»\nSUPABASE_ANON_KEY=«jwt»\nSUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=«supabase-publishable-key»\nSUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=«supabase-secret-key»

case:     a publishable key written straight after a secret key
in:       sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567sb_publishable_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-secret-key»«supabase-publishable-key»

case:     a secret key written straight after an access token
in:       sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «supabase-access-token»«supabase-secret-key»

case:     a secret key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.sb_secret_0123456789abcdef012345_01234567
out:      «jwt»

# A Stripe prefix written against the end of a Supabase token, which ends the
# way the case named "a stripe prefix written against the end of a notion token"
# does and for the reason given there: a Supabase body is read to a count longer
# than the run the Stripe scan reads as a key written against a key, so both
# values are located in the one pass and neither is left in the text. Neither
# pattern's own file states what the two come to together, which is why the case
# is here.

case:     a stripe prefix written against the end of a supabase token
in:       sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «supabase-access-token»«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a stripe key a space away from a supabase token
in:       sbp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «supabase-access-token» «stripe-secret-key»

# A RubyGems API key beside the others, and the credentials written where a
# body would stand. This is where the block for every other pattern shows a
# value nested inside one, and the two cases below are the far side of that: a
# body is written in the sixteen characters a lowercase digest is, so an access
# key ID and a Google API key are each located where they stand and the prefix
# in front of them stays in the text.
#
# What a key does nest with is the patterns whose own alphabet reaches it. A
# classic GitHub token's body and an npm access token's are base62, so either
# runs through the eight letters of the prefix and stops at the underscore
# behind them; the spans overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to
# whichever starts earliest. A JWT signature and a Vault body are base64url,
# which holds the underscore too, so either covers a key written after it whole.
#
# Behind a key the count is what decides, as it is behind an access key ID: what
# is written after the fifty-seventh character keeps a redaction of its own or
# none.

case:     an access key id where a body would begin
in:       rubygems_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      rubygems_«aws-access-key-id»0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     a google api key where a body would begin
in:       rubygems_AIza0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy012345678
out:      rubygems_«google-api-key»012345678

case:     a rubygems key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       rubygems=rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      rubygems=«rubygems-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     a rubygems key written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzrubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a rubygems key
in:       rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «rubygems-api-key»«github-token»

case:     a rubygems key written straight after an npm access token
in:       npm_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzrubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «npm-access-token»

case:     a notion token written straight after a rubygems key
in:       rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefntn_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:      «rubygems-api-key»«notion-api-token»

case:     a rubygems key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «jwt»

case:     a rubygems key behind a vault prefix
in:       hvs.rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «hashicorp-vault-token»

case:     an environment file holding a rubygems key among the others
in:       RUBYGEMS_API_KEY=rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      RUBYGEMS_API_KEY=«rubygems-api-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Stripe prefix written against the end of a RubyGems key, which ends the way
# the case named "a stripe prefix written against the end of a notion token"
# does and for the reason given there: a RubyGems body is read to a count longer
# than the run the Stripe scan reads as a key written against a key, and it
# carries nothing that would break that run, so both values are located in the
# one pass. Neither pattern's own file states what the two come to together,
# which is why the case is here.

case:     a stripe prefix written against the end of a rubygems key
in:       rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «rubygems-api-key»«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a stripe key a space away from a rubygems key
in:       rubygems_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «rubygems-api-key» «stripe-secret-key»

# An OpenRouter API key beside the others, and inside them. A key opens sk-, as
# an OpenAI key and an Anthropic key do, and what tells the three apart is what
# stands behind that: sixty-four hexadecimal digits behind sk-or-v1- here, the
# eight characters T3BlbkFJ inside a run there, and a kind named between sk-ant-
# and its body for the third. The first three cases are the three written on one
# line, each keeping a redaction of its own.
#
# Then the two shapes where a key and something else cover one stretch of text.
# A key written in front of the OpenAI marker is inside an OpenAI run — every
# character of sk-or-v1- and of a body belongs to the base64url alphabet a run
# is read in — so the run reaches from the same sk- past the marker, and what
# comes out is one redaction reaching further than the key does. A key written
# in the signature of a JWT is the same shape from the other side. Neither
# leaves a piece of the key in the text, which is what these two are here for.
#
# Behind a key the count is what decides, as it is behind an access key ID: what
# is written after the seventy-third character keeps a redaction of its own or
# none. In front of one nothing does, and the classic GitHub token below shows
# it — a GitHub body is read to the end of its run and the sk of the prefix is
# written in that run's own alphabet, so the two spans overlap and the line
# comes out as one redaction rather than two.

case:     an openrouter key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       openrouter=sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      openrouter=«openrouter-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an openrouter key and an openai api key on one line
in:       OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef
out:      OPENROUTER_API_KEY=«openrouter-api-key» OPENAI_API_KEY=«openai-api-key»

case:     an openrouter key and an anthropic api key on one line
in:       OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      OPENROUTER_API_KEY=«openrouter-api-key» ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=«anthropic-api-key»

case:     an openrouter key in front of the marker an openai key is read by
in:       sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefT3BlbkFJ0123456789abcdef
out:      «openai-api-key»

case:     an openrouter key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «jwt»

case:     a jwt directly after an openrouter key, which the dot keeps apart
in:       sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «openrouter-api-key».«jwt»

case:     an access key id written straight after an openrouter key
in:       sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefAKIA0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «openrouter-api-key»«aws-access-key-id»

case:     a classic github token written straight after an openrouter key
in:       sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «openrouter-api-key»«github-token»

case:     an openrouter key written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzsk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «github-token»

case:     an environment file holding an openrouter key among the others
in:       OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA0123456789ABCDEF\nGITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      OPENROUTER_API_KEY=«openrouter-api-key»\nAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=«aws-access-key-id»\nGITHUB_TOKEN=«github-token»

# A Stripe prefix written against the end of an OpenRouter key, which ends the
# way the case named "a stripe prefix written against the end of a notion token"
# does and for the reason given there: an OpenRouter body is read to a count
# longer than the run the Stripe scan reads as a key written against a key, the
# hyphens that would break such a run standing in the prefix in front of the
# body rather than in it, so both values are located in the one pass. Neither
# pattern's own file states what the two come to together, which is why the case
# is here.

case:     a stripe prefix written against the end of an openrouter key
in:       sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «openrouter-api-key»«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a stripe key a space away from an openrouter key
in:       sk-or-v1-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «openrouter-api-key» «stripe-secret-key»

# The Stripe patterns together. An API key and a webhook signing secret are
# written into the same environment file and are read by patterns with different
# rules about the byte in front, which is what the last two cases here are
# about: the key types Stripe's API keys open with can close a word and so are
# held to no letter and no digit standing in front of them, and whsec_ cannot
# and is held to nothing at all.
#
# Where a secret is written straight onto the end of a key the two spans overlap
# and are redacted as one, attributed to what starts earliest. Where a key is
# written straight onto the end of a secret the key opens nothing, because a
# letter stands in front of its prefix, and what the secret's own run does not
# reach over is left in the clear. That is the far side of the two rules meeting
# and it is here to be looked up rather than arrived at — neither pattern's own
# file states what the two of them come to when both are enabled.
#
# A redaction opening a prefix a value had closed is what leaves a second pass
# something to find, as the block above this one turns on. Here it goes the
# other way: the last case's out line carries no sk, because the secret's run
# reached over the key type, so there is no prefix left for a second pass to
# open and the body stays in the clear for good.

case:     a stripe environment file holding one of each
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567\nSTRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567\nSTRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»\nSTRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=«stripe-publishable-key»\nSTRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=«stripe-webhook-signing-secret»

case:     a signing secret written straight onto the end of a secret key
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567whsec_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a secret key written straight onto the end of a signing secret
in:       whsec_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-webhook-signing-secret»

# The two Cloudflare patterns, which read the two halves of one format: the same
# forty characters of secret and eight of checksum behind a prefix that says
# which credential it is. A caller running both gets each under its own name,
# which is what the boundary between them is for — a key carries everything the
# user holding it can do, where a token carries what it was scoped to.
#
# Written side by side, each keeps its own name and its own span, whether or not
# anything stands between them.

case:     a cloudflare key and a cloudflare token on one line
in:       CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY=cfk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=cfut_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY=«cloudflare-api-key» CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=«cloudflare-api-token»

case:     a cloudflare key and a cloudflare token with nothing between them
in:       cfk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefcfut_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «cloudflare-api-key»«cloudflare-api-token»

# They also reach into each other, and how far is settled by the prefix rather
# than chosen by either scan. Every prefix closes with an underscore that no
# body is written with, so the underscore has to fall past the first value's
# last character: the overlap is at most the characters in front of it, and they
# land in the checksum. Standing there they have to be hexadecimal, which stops
# cfk_ and cfut_ at cf, two characters, and cfat_ at cfa, three — and any
# position shallower than the deepest works as well, with more of the prefix
# falling past the value's last character. The four cases below are the deepest
# reach of each of the three prefixes and the shallowest of one, and in each of
# them the two spans overlap and are redacted as one, attributed to whichever
# starts earliest, which is the outer value.

case:     a cloudflare key beginning two characters inside a cloudflare token
in:       cfut_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567012345cfk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «cloudflare-api-token»

case:     a cloudflare key beginning one character inside a cloudflare token
in:       cfut_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345670123456cfk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «cloudflare-api-token»

case:     a cloudflare token beginning two characters inside a cloudflare key
in:       cfk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567012345cfut_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «cloudflare-api-key»

case:     an account owned cloudflare token beginning three characters inside a cloudflare key
in:       cfk_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456701234cfat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «cloudflare-api-key»

# A Groq API key beside the other kinds, and inside them. A body is base62 read
# to the end of its run, so a value written in an alphabet as narrow can stand
# inside one and is located there as well; the two spans overlap and are
# redacted as one, attributed to whichever starts earliest. The underscore is
# what ends a body rather than a count, so a value whose own prefix carries one
# begins after the run it interrupted — and the two still overlap, because that
# run reached the letters standing in front of the underscore. A dot ends a body
# as well, which is what keeps a JWT written straight after a key a value of its
# own.
#
# Read the other way round it is the prefix's own underscore that matters.
# base64url admits it where base62 does not, so a whole key can be written
# inside a JWT signature without ending it, and the spans overlap there too.

case:     a groq key beside a github token and a jwt
in:       groq=gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd github=ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      groq=«groq-api-key» github=«github-token» jwt=«jwt»

case:     an access key id inside a groq key body
in:       gsk_AKIA0123456789ABCDEF0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a groq key inside the signature of a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      «jwt»

case:     a classic github token written straight after a groq key
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «groq-api-key»

case:     a groq key written straight after a classic github token
in:       ghp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzgsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd
out:      «github-token»

case:     a jwt written straight after a groq key
in:       gsk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcd.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      «groq-api-key».«jwt»
